defects: V is introduced as an arbitrary/free function `Set α → ℝ` with no defining relationship to f — it is never asserted to equal `eVariationOn f`, so the theorem no longer states anything about total variation; it becomes a claim about an unconstrained function V, which is not the same proposition
Uses ℝ-valued V instead of the extended nonnegative real value (ℝ≥0∞) that eVariationOn actually returns, silently assuming finiteness
Weakens α's order structure from LinearOrder to Preorder, which is not sufficient to guarantee eVariationOn behaves as in the gold statement
Uses MetricSpace β instead of PseudoEMetricSpace E, narrowing the codomain space and changing edist to dist
Conclusion uses ordinary `dist` instead of `edist`, inconsistent with the extended-metric setting of the original

s and t are plain arguments rather than implicit, and x y are explicit rather than implicit — minor signature deviation, but combined with the missing V-f link this is a substantive formalization failure
